newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria warns of more bombs after written threat.
newsitem.headline: Austria warns of more bombs after written threat.

text.p: Austria's Interior Ministry sounded a new warning on Tuesday of possible letter-bomb attacks ahead of nationwide elections this month and revealed that an extremist group had sent a written threat to a news magazine.
An Interior Ministry spokesman said a group calling itself the Bajuvarian Liberation Army had written to current affairs magazine Profil warning of eight bombs.
Bajuvaria is an archaic term for the German state of Bavaria.
"The people named in the letter have been warned...We still do not know if the letter is authentic but we have reason to believe we should take it seriously," the spokesman said.
The letter bore a postmark from the south-eastern region of Styria and was posted on Friday.
The Interior Ministry had issued a first bomb warning on Sunday linked to European parliamentary elections and Vienna state elections on October 13.

Police believe neo-Nazi extremists are behind a series of bombings in Austria and Germany that have killed four and maimed at least 15 since December 1993. The authorities have failed to secure any convictions.
The Bajuvarian Liberation Army has claimed responsibility for more than 20 letter bombs directed against foreigners and figures linked to immigrant or refugee issues.
In December 1993, former Vienna mayor Helmut Zilk lost three fingers when he opened a letter bomb.
Last year four gypsies died in a bomb blast when a booby-trap exploded as they tried to remove a racist sign from their village.
